STEP 2 — TIME IN AIR  (only y knows when it lands: set y = 0)
The hand, foot or cannon was touching it — that push ends at release. Gravity needs no contact, so it keeps pulling down for the whole flight. Nothing keeps pushing it forward.

The horizontal motion never changes because nothing pushes sideways once the ball leaves the hand. Gravity only acts downward, so the vertical speed shrinks, reaches zero at the top, and grows again on the way down. That is why the path is symmetric when launch and landing are at the same height.
Open question: what changes if the ground is a slope instead of flat?
